description:
Return the other filings this filing cites. Call it after list_company_filings or get_filing_parsed, with the `aann_` id they returned, when you need the paper trail around a filing rather than the filing alone.

Chinese listed companies print a filing number on most of their filings (e.g. 2026-047) and later filings cite it in their text. This tool follows those citations. Matching is exact and scoped to the same company — those numbers are per-company yearly counters and collide across the market, so a cross-company match would be wrong, not merely noisy.

Unlike get_filing_parsed this has NO recency window: you can ask about a filing of any age. What comes back is title, date and id, so you can feed any `aann_` straight back into get_filing_parsed — that step is the one limited to recent filings.

Read the empty case carefully, because two different facts look similar. found=false means we hold no such filing id. found=true with an empty `related` means we do hold it and it cites nothing we have. `own_number` tells you the other half of the story: when it is null, this filing prints no number of its own, so nothing can cite it either. About a third of filings carry no printed number, so an empty result is ordinary rather than a sign of missing data.

WHERE COVERAGE ENDS: every filing whose text we hold has been scanned for citations, so an empty `related` on those is a real answer, not a gap. What is still incomplete is the corpus itself — a sizeable part of the archive is crawled but not yet parsed, and a filing we have not parsed cannot appear on either side of a citation. So a cited filing may be missing simply because we have not processed it yet, which is also why `matched_no` is worth reading: it names the number that was cited, even when we can only resolve some of them.

`aevt_` on an entry is null when the cited filing produced no event. That is normal: we extract only a few event types so far (list_coverage names them), and the citation link itself does not depend on extraction.

Do NOT use this to sweep a company or the market: it takes a single filing id, has no cursor, and follows citations one hop at a time. Do NOT expect the cited filing's text here either — this returns identity only; pass the `aann_` to get_filing_parsed for text, and note that step does have a recency window.

aann_.description: Opaque filing id from list_company_filings, e.g. aann_Kyw46MM1gCnIaBxA.
aann_.title: Aann

limit.description: Max related filings to return. See limits.related_limit_max.
limit.title: Limit

name: get_related_filings

outputSchema.description: Which other filings this filing cites, by printed filing number within the same company.

found.description: False means we hold no filing under this id at all. An empty `related` list with found=true is a different answer: we have the filing, it just does not cite any filing we hold.
found.title: Found

more_available.description: True when there may be more beyond `limit`. There is no cursor; raise limit (max in list_coverage) if you need more.
more_available.title: More Available

own_number.description: This filing's OWN printed number, or null when its text does not carry one (about a third do not). This is also why other filings may fail to link here: without a printed number there is nothing for them to cite.
own_number.title: Own Number

related.description: Newest first. Each entry includes {aann_, title, ann_date, matched_no, extractions, aevt_, event_type}. matched_no is the printed number that tied the two together. extractions is the complete event list; aevt_ and event_type are a single compatibility representative. They are null when the cited filing produced no event. See list_coverage for supported types.
related.title: Related

outputSchema.title: RelatedFilingsResult
